purpose: the 262144 promotion gate proved retrieval works at depth but left decode throughput and DSpark acceptance at depth unmeasured; every 28-48 tok/s figure we had came from 2-5k prompts

method.generation: 400 tokens per point, above SGLang's decode_log_interval=40 so decode telemetry actually emits; earlier probes generated 13 tokens and produced no telemetry at all
method.separation: streamed TTFT splits prefill from decode, rather than dividing total wall clock and blending the two
method.filler: varied generated records, not repeated blocks, which the radix cache would collapse into an unrepresentative prefix hit
method.task: identical prose task at every depth, so the depth comparison is like-for-like; prose has the lowest DSpark acceptance of the content types, so these are conservative decode numbers

dspark_accept_len_by_depth.conclusion: flat with depth. Speculative decoding does not collapse at long context, so the decode slowdown is attention cost, not draft-model failure.

radix_prefix_reuse.method: one ~98k body sent three times: cold, then identical prefix with a different trailing question, then the same length with a single token altered at record 2 (~0.1% into the body)
radix_prefix_reuse.conclusion: reuse is near-total but strictly prefix-anchored. An identical prefix turns 98k tokens of prefill into 0.53s. Changing one token near the top forfeits all of it, even though 99.9% of the content is unchanged.

operational_consequences.long_context_is_cheap_to_hold_expensive_: decode falls only 25% (21.9 -> 16.4 tok/s) across a 100x context increase, while prefill throughput falls 68% and TTFT goes superlinear. At 230k, 93% of wall clock is prefill (313s of 338s).
operational_consequences.design_rule: do not minimize prompt size; minimize prefix churn. Pay for the context once and never invalidate it.
operational_consequences.anti_patterns: anything that mutates the head of the prompt per attempt costs a full prefill every time: embedded timestamps, attempt or retry counters, elapsed-time banners, reordered tool lists, a rotating system preamble. At 230k that is ~5 minutes per attempt, paid repeatedly overnight.
